Who we are 

At Twilio, we’re shaping the future of communications, all from the comfort of our homes. We deliver innovative solutions to hundreds of thousands of businesses and empower millions of developers worldwide to craft personalized customer experiences.

Our dedication to remote-first work, and strong culture of connection and global inclusion means that no matter your location, you’re part of a vibrant team with diverse experiences making a global impact each day. As we continue to revolutionize how the world interacts, we’re acquiring new skills and experiences that make work feel truly rewarding. Your career at Twilio is in your hands.
.

Hiring and how we work

We use Artificial Intelligence (AI) to help make our hiring process efficient. That said, every hiring decision is made by real Twilions! 

Also, while we are a remote-first company, you may be asked to report in person on an ad-hoc basis for team gatherings, functional off-sites or customer meetings. 
.

See yourself at Twilio

Join the team as Twilio’s next Marketing Strategy & Planning Manager.

About the job

We're hiring a Marketing Strategy & Analytics Manager to join our global marketing analytics team, sitting alongside our Media Mix Modeling (MMM) data scientists and our regional analytics business partners (EMEA and APJ). This is a hybrid role: part senior business partner, part data scientist. You'll act as a trusted analytics advisor to marketing leadership — owning end-to-end analyses of funnel performance, campaign effectiveness, and marketing ROI — while also being fluent enough in MMM methodology to apply, extend, and translate our MMM outputs into decisions our regional and global marketing leaders can act on.

This role is ideal for someone who has grown from a strong analytics/BI background into applied data science, has direct exposure to MMM (Robyn, Meridian, or similar), and wants a role that blends storytelling and stakeholder influence with genuine modeling depth.

Responsibilities

In this role, you’ll:

  • Strategy & Analytics Partnership: Act as the trusted analytics advisor to global and regional marketing leaders, translating business questions into analyses that shape budget, channel, and campaign decisions.
  • MMM Application & Translation: Apply and extend outputs from our MMM data science team — interpreting model results, running scenario/what-if analyses, and adapting them for regional nuance and stakeholder-specific questions.
  • Measurement & Funnel Analytics: Build and maintain incremental analyses that complement MMM (geo-lift tests, channel-level diagnostics, funnel and pipeline analytics) to validate and enrich model-driven recommendations. Own end-to-end analytics across B2B and B2C marketing funnels, from data pull through insight to executive-ready recommendation.
  • MMM Team Partnership: Partner closely with the central MMM data science team to ensure model assumptions, inputs, and outputs reflect real business context, and to prioritize the roadmap of modeling questions that matter most to the business.
  • Tooling & Scale: Write production-quality Python/SQL for data pulls, analysis, and light modeling; build reusable tools and dashboards that scale insight generation across the team.
  • Storytelling & Communication: Craft and deliver clear, compelling narratives and presentations for senior stakeholders across Marketing, Sales, Product, and Finance.
  • Cross-Regional Collaboration: Partner with regional analytics business partners (EMEA, APJ) to ensure consistency.

Qualifications 

Twilio values diverse experiences from all kinds of industries, and we encourage everyone who meets the required qualifications to apply. If your career is just starting or hasn't followed a traditional path, don't let that stop you from considering Twilio. We are always looking for people who will bring something new to the table!

*Required:

  • The Hybrid Analyst: 6+ years of experience in marketing analytics, business intelligence, or data science, with a track record of directly influencing marketing strategy through data.
  • Technically Fluent: Strong proficiency in Python and SQL for analysis; comfortable working with large, messy marketing datasets.
  • MMM-Literate: Hands-on exposure to Media Mix Modeling concepts and at least one MMM tool or framework (e.g., Robyn, Meridian, or an equivalent regression/econometric approach) — you don't need to have built an MMM from scratch, but you can interpret, apply, and reason about one.
  • Statistically Grounded: Solid grounding in statistics and experimental design (e.g., regression, A/B testing, geo-lift/incrementality testing).
  • The Trusted Advisor: Demonstrated ability to partner with senior stakeholders (Marketing, Sales, Finance) and turn analysis into decisions — not just dashboards.
  • Storyteller: Excellent communication and storytelling skills; experience presenting to both technical and executive, non-technical audiences.
  • Channel Fluency: Solid understanding of digital and traditional media channels and B2B/B2C marketing funnels. 

Desired:

  • Prior direct experience building or co-building an MMM model, or working as an embedded analytics partner to an MMM/data science team.
  • Experience working on or with AI products (e.g., LLMs, copilots, RAG apps, workflow tools).
  • Prior experience in B2B marketing analytics, consulting, or an agency environment.
  • Experience working across multiple regions or in a global, matrixed organization.
  • Specify education, previous job experience, certifications, technical skills and soft skills required. 

Location

This role will be remotely based in India (Karnataka, Tamil Nadu, Telangana, Maharashtra or Delhi).

Travel 

We prioritize connection and opportunities to build relationships with our customers and each other. For this role, you may be required to travel occasionally to participate in project or team in-person meetings.

What We Offer

Working at Twilio offers many benefits, including competitive pay, generous time off, ample parental and wellness leave, healthcare, a retirement savings program, and much more. Offerings vary by location.

Twilio thinks big. Do you?

We like to solve problems, take initiative, pitch in when needed, and are always up for trying new things. That's why we seek out colleagues who embody our values — something we call Twilio Magic. Additionally, we empower employees to build positive change in their communities by supporting their volunteering and donation efforts.

So, if you're ready to unleash your full potential, do your best work, and be the best version of yourself, apply now! If this role isn't what you're looking for, please consider other open positions.

Who We Are
Notion is the collaborative AI workspace where teams and agents think together . We're building one place where your knowledge, projects, meetings, and AI tools live side by side, so work is faster, clearer, and less fragmented. Millions of individuals, small teams, and large companies run their work on Notion.

Notinos (our employees) are customer zero in bringing this future of work to life. We care about craft, building things that last, and the belief that great work is still fundamentally human. Our goal isn’t to ship the next feature. Each and every team of Notinos is working to set the standard for how humans work together in the AI era. From building a business’s system of record to making and managing AI agents to automating away the busy work, we care deeply about giving our customers more time for their life’s work.

About the Role:
Notion is looking for a Forward Deployed Engineer focused on migrations to join our growing team in India. You will help deliver complex, production-grade data migrations, integrations, and automations for customers across APAC.
This is initially an internally focused, hands-on engineering role. You will partner closely with regional Forward Deployed Engineers, who own customer discovery, solution architecture, stakeholder communication, risk management, and final customer validation. You will own the behind-the-scenes technical execution layer from feasibility assessment and implementation through testing, production rollout, QA, reconciliation, reporting, and operational handoff.
You will work across multiple customer environments and source systems, often with incomplete requirements, imperfect data, and real-world constraints. Success requires strong engineering fundamentals, sound judgment, careful validation, and the ability to turn one-off delivery work into reusable tools and repeatable playbooks.
As a founding engineer in India, you will help build a new regional engineering capability from the ground up. You will create migration infrastructure, standards, and reusable tooling used by FDEs across APAC, while establishing practices that can scale globally. The role offers an opportunity to become a technical authority for production migration delivery, shaping how Notion approaches reliability, validation, and operational quality across complex customer environments. As the team grows, the role may also expand toward customer-facing FDE work, technical leadership, or a deeper engineering path, depending on business needs and demonstrated capability.

What You'll Achieve:
• Own the technical execution layer after customer requirements, scope, and solution architecture have been established with the regional FDE. Contribute to feasibility assessment, estimation, implementation planning, and risk identification while the regional FDE remains accountable for customer discovery, scope, architecture, stakeholder communication, and final acceptance.

• Apply a repeatable migration lifecycle covering source inventory and sampling, scope and pruning decisions, compatibility and degradation assessment, transformation design, pilot or dry run, user acceptance testing, production cutover, reconciliation, remediation, hypercare, and documented handoff.

• Translate approved customer and regional FDE requirements into clear technical designs, implementation plans, test strategies, runbooks, and delivery estimates.

• Build production-quality migration utilities, backend services, data pipelines, integrations, and automations using Python, SQL, APIs, databases, and cloud infrastructure.

• Investigate source-system behavior, data quality issues, permissions, rate limits, authentication constraints, and edge cases, then recommend practical solutions.

• Design and validate permissions, ownership, and inheritance mappings against the approved migration plan. Make unsupported or ambiguous access requirements explicit, obtain the required decision or approval, and preserve evidence of validation.

• Design migrations for reliability, scale, security, observability, idempotency, failure recovery, and safe reruns.

• Execute migrations only through approved environments, devices, accounts, and tooling. Follow least-privilege access, customer-specific security and data-residency requirements, and approved handling procedures. Do not store customer data in unmanaged local or external systems, and escalate privacy, security, or sovereignty concerns before execution.

• Build validation and reconciliation frameworks that provide clear evidence of migration completeness, accuracy, and exceptions.

• Debug failures across application code, infrastructure, customer data, third-party systems, and the Notion platform, then drive issues through resolution.

• Manage multiple implementation workstreams, dependencies, and priorities while communicating scope, progress, risks, and trade-offs clearly.

• Surface scope changes, unsupported requirements, timeline risks, and material effort increases early. Document assumptions and trade-offs, and escalate with options and a recommended path rather than silently absorbing additional work.

• Maintain an auditable record of scope, decisions, risks, approvals, validation evidence, and customer acceptance criteria in the agreed shared workspace or channel.

• Convert repeated delivery patterns into reusable components, automation, documentation, and playbooks that improve speed, quality, and cost over time.

• Bring field learnings back to Notion's Product and Engineering teams as actionable platform feedback and technical requirements.

Skills You'll Need to Bring:
• 3 to 6 years of hands-on experience in backend engineering, data engineering, integration engineering, implementation engineering, technical consulting, solutions engineering, or a similar technical role.

• Strong hands-on Python development experience.

• Working experience with Node.js, JavaScript, or TypeScript.

• Strong SQL skills and a solid understanding of relational databases, data modeling, and data transformation.

• Experience working with REST APIs, JSON, authentication, webhooks, and system integrations.

• Experience owning a production migration, integration, or technical implementation through mapping, transformation, testing, rollout, validation, and handoff.

• Experience taking a technical problem from requirements and design through development, testing, deployment, and production operation.

• Experience with Git, code review, automated testing, release practices, and production deployment.

• Strong debugging, analytical, and problem-solving skills across code, data, infrastructure, and external systems.

• Evidence of working on production systems, not only prototypes or proof-of-concept projects.

• Clear written and verbal English communication, with the ability to explain technical decisions, constraints, and risks to technical and non-technical stakeholders.

• High agency and ownership. You are comfortable making progress with incomplete information, challenging assumptions, and escalating with options and a recommendation.

Nice to Haves:
• Experience with Docker, Kubernetes, CI/CD, job orchestration, or infrastructure automation.

• Experience with AWS, GCP, or Azure.

• Familiarity with message queues, event-driven systems, distributed-system patterns, retries, concurrency, and rate limits.

• Experience with monitoring, logging, alerting, or other observability tools.

• Experience with enterprise SaaS applications, professional services, or large-scale customer implementations.

• Experience migrating large volumes of content or structured data between enterprise platforms.

• Experience with AI or LLM applications, retrieval-augmented generation, evaluation frameworks, or agentic workflows.

• Familiarity with MCP, tool calling, Notion Workers, Custom Agents, or similar extensibility platforms.

• Experience working with distributed global or APAC teams.

What success looks like:
In your first 90 days, you will:
• Learn Notion's migration and implementation ecosystem, engineering standards, and APAC delivery model.

• Establish a productive working rhythm with regional FDE partners.

• Contribute to at least one migration or integration workstream through production delivery.

• Leave behind clear technical documentation, validation evidence, and an operational runbook.

Within your first six months, you will:
• Independently own production migration or integration workstreams from technical design through rollout and handoff.

• Deliver measurable improvements in migration turnaround time, validation quality, delivery cost, or regional FDE execution hours through reusable engineering.

• Help establish repeatable quality controls, code review practices, runbooks, and observability patterns for the India team.

• Demonstrate effective prioritization and communication across multiple concurrent APAC engagements.

This role is based in New York. We use a hybrid work model of 3 days in the office per week. We offer relocation assistance. Travel up to 50% may be required.

In this role, you will
• Design and ship production AI systems around models, owning integrations, data flows, reliability, observability, and on-call readiness across financial workflows.

• Lead discovery and scoping from pre-sales through post-production, translating ambiguous business problems into hypothesis-driven problem framing, system requirements, and delivery plans with measurable outcomes.

A World-Changing Company

Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

The Role

Palantir builds applications that help customers organize, understand, and make decisions based on their data. Because these applications serve different roles within an organization's workflow, users frequently have multiple applications open at once, and expect them to work together seamlessly. While backend services handle much of this coordination, delivering a truly fast and responsive experience requires applications to also directly interact with each other through client-side frameworks running in the browser. Building these frameworks is uniquely challenging: every Palantir application plays a distinct role and has its own set of first-class UX concepts, yet the frameworks need to integrate cleanly into all of them. Success requires both strong API design skills and a keen eye for user experience.

The frontend frameworks our team builds serve a variety of functions across Palantir's application ecosystem. Some frameworks integrate deeply with the Palantir Ontology—a foundational layer that provides a schema for defining objects and relationships between them. These frameworks enable real-time data synchronization across applications: for example, when a user selects an Ontology object on a map, data plots in a different application instantly update to show that object's properties. Other frameworks operate independently of the Ontology: for example, one framework allows applications to define custom behaviors that can be invoked by other applications or even by AI agents, giving them the flexibility to expose arbitrary functionality across the platform.

Core Responsibilities

As a software engineer on this team, you'll work with these cross-application frameworks end-to-end, from the low-level technical implementation to high-level UX decisions. You'll work extensively with core web APIs—Broadcast Channels, Service Workers, Local Storage—to enable real-time communication between applications. Additionally, you will help develop an Electron application that extends and enhances these workflows through Electron-specific capabilities, such as the IPC API. Along the way, you'll build relationships with teams across the company and develop a deep understanding of different codebases and their architectural patterns.

API design is central to the role: the interfaces you create need to be ergonomic and portable enough to slot into any application that adopts them, while also being powerful enough to enable complex user interactions. Just as important is a strong sense and passion for UX: the interactions these frameworks enable should feel native and intuitive regardless of which applications a user has open. The ideal candidate is a well-rounded engineer who is excited by the creative challenge of designing new cross-app behaviors, and has the technical know-how to codify these behaviors in an idiomatic and extensible way.
